external_evidence.label: FL-511 2026 Point-in-Time and Housing Inventory Count
external_evidence.geography: Pensacola/Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties Continuum of Care
external_evidence.source_values: The FL-511 January 26, 2026 count reported 1,150 people experiencing homelessness: 311 in emergency shelter, 416 in transitional housing, and 423 unsheltered. Adult-only households accounted for 1,124 people, including 410 unsheltered adults. The report identified 248 people experiencing chronic homelessness, including 214 who were unsheltered.
external_evidence.executive_language: The FL-511 January 2026 Point-in-Time Count documented 1,150 people experiencing homelessness across the Pensacola/Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties CoC, including 423 people who were unsheltered.
external_evidence.application_language: The FL-511 January 26, 2026 Point-in-Time Count documented 1,150 people experiencing homelessness across the Pensacola/Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties Continuum of Care: 311 in emergency shelter, 416 in transitional housing, and 423 unsheltered. Adult-only households accounted for 1,124 people, including 410 unsheltered adults; 248 people met the chronic-homelessness definition, including 214 who were unsheltered.
external_evidence.caveat: A PIT count is a single-night snapshot across the two-county CoC and must not be described as annual prevalence or as an Escambia-only count.

application_questions.label: Executive Summary and Publix Fit
application_questions.prompt: Summarize the organization, proposed housing and shelter request, population served, geography, and alignment with Publix Charities' housing focus.

application_questions.label: Community Need
application_questions.prompt: Describe the housing insecurity and homelessness need Broken Growth is positioned to address, who is affected, and why a combined housing and reentry response matters.

application_questions.label: Housing and Shelter Program Design
application_questions.prompt: Describe the proposed housing and shelter model, participant supports, admission approach, safety structure, and path from immediate stability toward independence.

application_questions.label: Goals and Measurable Objectives
application_questions.prompt: State the project goals, first-phase objectives, planned capacity, implementation dependencies, and measurable participant or program targets.

application_questions.label: Outcomes and Evaluation
application_questions.prompt: Explain the outputs and outcomes Broken Growth will track, the data sources it will use, and how it will distinguish projections from achieved results.

application_questions.label: Organizational Capacity
application_questions.prompt: Describe Broken Growth's legal standing, mission, leadership, governance, current service activity, and readiness to develop the housing program responsibly.

application_questions.label: Project Readiness and Risk Controls
application_questions.prompt: Describe the proposed site and development phase, what is known, what still requires zoning, engineering, site-control, vendor, budget, or board confirmation, and how those risks will be managed.

application_questions.label: Community Partnerships
application_questions.prompt: Describe confirmed housing, shelter, reentry, workforce, behavioral-health, faith, employer, transportation, or referral partners and each partner's role.

application_questions.label: Financial and Program Sustainability
application_questions.prompt: Explain how the housing and shelter work will be sustained through diversified revenue, responsible resident contributions if approved, partnerships, and disciplined cost and outcome management.

application_questions.label: Request Amount and Use of Funds
application_questions.prompt: State the exact amount requested from Publix, the allowable housing or shelter costs it will support, the basis for each line item, other committed or prospective funds, and how the request budget reconciles to the project plan.

submission_steps: Confirm that an authorized Broken Growth employee, board member, or decision maker will own the Publix account and application.
On a current desktop browser, register the organization or log in; if the 501(c)(3) determination remains pending, follow Publix's official FAQ and answer No to the EIN question.
Capture the exact live application prompts, character limits, required attachments, allowable uses, certifications, and any deadline time or timezone.
Return the captured prompts to GrantBot, map each prepared narrative to the exact field, and resolve every hard gate without inventing facts.
Set a right-sized request amount, complete the line-item budget from current quotes or documented assumptions, and obtain board or authorized-officer approval.
Run final claim, eligibility, budget, attachment, and consistency reviews; proofread the complete portal preview before submission.
Have the authorized human make all certifications and submit no later than August 31, 2026; save the submitted copy and confirmation number.
Because Publix states submitted applications cannot be edited in the portal, email the designated Publix contact if a correction becomes necessary rather than submitting a duplicate.
